name: ht_next
prose: void *ht_next(struct ht_iter *iter) (lib9p hashtable.c lines 251-267; the packet name ht_iter_next is not the real name). Precondition: iter was initialised with ht_iter and its parent table is alive. Postcondition: if iter->htit_next holds a pre-located next item (set by ht_remove_at_iter) it is used and htit_next is cleared with no lock taken; otherwise it takes the parent table's read lock, calls ht_iter_advance(iter, iter->htit_curr) to find the item after the current one (this also updates iter->htit_slot as it scans the buckets), and releases the lock. iter->htit_curr is set to that item (NULL once the iteration is exhausted) and the function returns the item's hti_data pointer, or NULL if there is no further item. The caller keeps no lock or reference.
note: slice cut head; real name ht_next (hashtable.c:252); added htit_slot side effect

name: l9p_pufcall
prose: int l9p_pufcall(struct l9p_message *msg, union l9p_fcall *fcall, enum l9p_version version) (lib9p pack.c lines 434-868; the packet name l9p_pack_fcall is not the real name). It both packs and unpacks, depending on msg->lm_mode (L9P_PACK or L9P_UNPACK); I read the whole function, but not the l9p_pu* helpers beyond their header comments. Precondition: msg is set up for the chosen direction, fcall is valid (zeroed when unpacking) and, when packing, fcall->hdr.type is the message to write. Postcondition: it first transfers the 4-byte length (a local zero placeholder, ignored when unpacking), the type byte and the 16-bit tag; if the tag transfer returns negative it returns -1. Then it transfers the type-specific fields in protocol order with l9p_pu8/16/32/64, l9p_pustring(s) and l9p_puqid(s); for some types a field is transferred only when version >= L9P_2000U (TAUTH n_uname, TATTACH n_uname, RERROR errnum, TCREATE extension). For types with no body (RFLUSH, RCLUNK, RREMOVE, RWSTAT, RRENAME, RSETATTR, RXATTRCREATE, RFSYNC, RLINK, RRENAMEAT, RUNLINKAT) nothing more is transferred; for an unknown type it logs 'missing case for type' and transfers nothing more. The status r checked afterwards is the result of the last primitive of the case (or of an early-checked string); results of intermediate primitives are ignored. If r < 0 it returns -1 (not an errno); when unpacking, memory may already have been allocated and the caller must call l9p_freefcall. Otherwise, when packing, it rewinds the message cursor to the start, subtracts the 4 length bytes from lm_size, computes len = lm_size (plus io.count for RREAD/RREADDIR, whose data is added separately), and writes len over the first four bytes; when unpacking nothing more is done. It returns 0. Note that TWSTAT packs an uninitialised 16-bit size local and RSTAT packs the size from l9p_sizeof_stat.
note: old prose said negative errno from the first failing primitive and r-on-entry for body-less cases; actual: -1 and r holds the tag transfer result

name: bsdcat_getopt
prose: int bsdcat_getopt(struct bsdcat *bsdcat) (libarchive cat/cmdline.c lines 93-270). The short option string is "h" (no short option takes an argument) and the only long options are "help" (equivalent 'h') and "version" (equivalent OPTION_VERSION), neither takes an argument. Precondition: bsdcat->argv is a NULL-terminated array, argc matches, getopt_state is 0 (start) on the first call and otherwise the state left by the previous call. Postcondition: on the first call the program name word is skipped; it returns -1 when no words remain, when the next word does not begin with '-', or when the next word is exactly "--" (which is consumed). A word beginning with a single '-' is parsed as a group of short options, one per call (a lone "-" word is consumed without returning anything and parsing continues with the next word); a short option not in the table returns '?' silently, with no warning; 'h' returns 'h'. A word beginning with '--' is looked up in the long table (name up to an optional '='): an unsupported or ambiguous name, or an argument given with '=' to an option that forbids one, prints a lafe_warnc message and returns '?'; a unique match returns its equivalent, which is 'h' for --help or OPTION_VERSION for --version. bsdcat->argument is NULL except when set from '=' text (which causes an error here), argv/argc advance past consumed words, and the parser state is updated for the next call. The code paths for required arguments and for the -W form exist but cannot be reached with this option table.
note: reviewers: R1 (unknown short option silent) RIGHT, R15 (--version returns OPTION_VERSION, not a short character) RIGHT

name: UpdateModel
prose: static void UpdateModel(CPpmd7 *p) (archive_ppmd7.c lines 459-606; slice cut head). Precondition: the model is initialised and p->FoundState, p->MinContext, p->MaxContext and p->OrderFall describe the symbol just coded. Postcondition: returns nothing. Step 1: if p->FoundState->Freq < MAX_FREQ/4 and MinContext has a suffix, the entry for the same symbol in the suffix context c is adjusted: a single-state context gets Freq++ only if Freq < 32; otherwise the matching state is found (assumed present), swapped one place forward if its Freq is not below its predecessor's, and, if its Freq < MAX_FREQ-9, gets Freq += 2 and c->SummFreq += 2; if the condition is false none of this is done. Step 2: if p->OrderFall == 0 the function sets MinContext = MaxContext = CreateSuccessors(p, True); if that is NULL it calls RestartModel and returns, otherwise it makes FoundState's successor point at that context and returns; in this branch nothing is appended to p->Text and no states are added to contexts. Step 3 (OrderFall != 0): it appends FoundState->Symbol to Text and, if Text >= UnitsStart, calls RestartModel and returns. If the found state has a successor, and that successor is not above the new text position it calls CreateSuccessors(p, False) (NULL -> RestartModel and return) to get a real context; then it decrements OrderFall and, if that reaches 0, makes the text position's successor the new context and moves Text back by one when MaxContext != MinContext. If the found state has no successor, its successor is set to the text position and the successor context is taken as MinContext. Step 4: for each context from MaxContext along suffix links up to (excluding) MinContext it makes room for one more state (expanding the stats block or converting a one-state context into a stats array; an allocation failure calls RestartModel and returns), adjusts SummFreq and appends a state for the symbol with a computed Freq and the successor. Finally MaxContext = MinContext = the successor context.
note: reviewers: R1 (suffix update conditional) RIGHT and R15 (OrderFall==0 branch skips Text/context updates) RIGHT; old prose described only the main path

name: UpdateModel
prose: static void UpdateModel(CPpmd8 *p) (archive_ppmd8.c lines 805-972). Precondition: the model is initialised and FoundState, MinContext, MaxContext, OrderFall describe the symbol just coded. Postcondition: returns nothing. Step 1: as in ppmd7, if FoundState->Freq < MAX_FREQ/4 and MinContext has a suffix, the suffix context's state s for that symbol is updated (single-state context: Freq++ when < 32; otherwise swap forward when Freq >= predecessor's, then Freq += 2 and SummFreq += 2 when Freq < MAX_FREQ-9); s is remembered for later. Step 2: with c = the saved MaxContext, if OrderFall == 0 and the found state has a successor, it calls CreateSuccessors(p, True, s, MinContext): on NULL it clears FoundState's successor and calls RESTORE_MODEL(c, CTX(fSuccessor)); otherwise it sets FoundState's successor to the new context and sets MaxContext to it (MinContext is not changed); either way it returns. Step 3: otherwise it appends the symbol to Text first and then, if Text >= UnitsStart, calls RESTORE_MODEL(c, CTX(fSuccessor)) and returns. Step 4: if the found state has no successor it calls ReduceOrder(p, s, MinContext) (NULL -> RESTORE_MODEL(c, 0), return); else if the successor points below UnitsStart it calls CreateSuccessors(p, False, s, MinContext) (NULL -> RESTORE_MODEL(c, 0), return). Step 5: it decrements OrderFall; at 0 the successor becomes the new context and Text moves back one when MaxContext != MinContext; otherwise, with PPMD8_FREEZE_SUPPORT and RestoreMethod above FREEZE, the successor becomes the new context, text is reset and OrderFall set to 0. Step 6: for each context c from the saved MaxContext up to (excluding) MinContext it expands or creates the stats array and appends a state for the symbol; if an allocation fails it calls RESTORE_MODEL(c, CTX(fSuccessor)) with that current loop context c (not the saved MaxContext) and returns. Finally MaxContext = MinContext = CTX(fSuccessor).
note: reviewers: R1 (early returns leave MinContext unchanged) RIGHT; R15 (allocation-failure RESTORE_MODEL uses loop context c; Text append precedes UnitsStart check) RIGHT

name: archive_check_magic
note: archive_check_magic is a function-like macro (archive_private.h:150-156) whose body does 'return ARCHIVE_FATAL' in the caller; the function it forwards to, __archive_check_magic, is defined in archive_check_magic.c, outside this slice

name: arc4_addrandom
prose: static inline void arc4_addrandom(uint8_t *dat, int datlen) (archive_random.c lines 203-218; operates on the file-static struct arc4_stream rs). Precondition: datlen > 0 (dat[n % datlen] is evaluated for n = 0..255), dat points to datlen readable bytes, and rs.s is an initialised 256-byte array; the caller (arc4_stir) is expected to hold the arc4random lock. Postcondition: rs.i is first decremented and then incremented once in each of 256 loop iterations (all as uint8_t), so its final value is the original value minus 1 modulo 256; in each iteration rs.j is advanced by rs.s[rs.i] plus a byte of dat and the two entries rs.s[rs.i] and rs.s[rs.j] are swapped, so rs.s stays a permutation of its previous contents; finally rs.j is set equal to rs.i. Nothing is returned and no memory is allocated or freed.
note: reviewers: R2 (net decrement by 1, datlen=0 is a division by zero) RIGHT; R15 (final rs.i equals original) WRONG: 256 increments after one decrement leave i = i0 - 1 mod 256 (lines 209-217)

name: __archive_read_next_passphrase
prose: const char *__archive_read_next_passphrase(struct archive_read *a) (archive_read_add_passphrase.c lines 137-189). Precondition: a->passphrases.candidate is -1 (after __archive_read_reset_passphrase) or a count between 0 and the number of passphrases in the list (it is decremented while the list length stays the same); when candidate == 1 the list must be non-empty. Postcondition: if candidate < 0 it counts the list, sets candidate to the count and picks the first passphrase; else if candidate > 1 it decrements candidate, moves the head to the tail and picks the new head; else if candidate == 1 it sets candidate to 0, rotates the list once if it has more than one element, and picks none; else (candidate 0) picks none. If a passphrase was picked its string (owned by the archive's list) is returned. Otherwise, if a callback is set, it calls it; if the callback returns non-NULL, a copy (malloc + strdup) is inserted at the head of the list, candidate is set to 1, and the callback's own string pointer (not the copy) is returned; if copying fails an ENOMEM error is set and NULL is returned; if the callback returns NULL, NULL is returned. With no callback and nothing picked, NULL is returned.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): precondition 'candidate equals list length' was false after rotation; reviewer R1 claim (NULL when exhausted even if callback supplies) already handled

name: find_elf_data_sec
prose: static ssize_t find_elf_data_sec(struct archive_read *a) (archive_read_support_format_7zip.c lines 744-882; slice shows lines 757-882). Precondition: a is a reader positioned at the start of a candidate file. Postcondition: returns the file offset of the section header's data (sh_offset) of the ELF section named ".data" when every step succeeds: the first 0x40 bytes begin with the ELF magic, the section header table fields satisfy e_shnum >= e_shstrndx and e_shentsize >= 0x28 (64-bit) or 0x18 (32-bit), seeking to the table and the string table and reading them succeeds, strtab_size is between 6 and SIZE_MAX, the string ".data\0" is found in the string table by a loop that only examines offsets below strtab_size - 6, a section whose name offset equals that position is found, and its offset is at most SSIZE_MAX. In every other case (not ELF, bad header values, seek or read failure, no name match, no section, offset too large) it returns the default SFX_MIN_ADDR. Before returning it always seeks the stream back to offset 0 (the seek result is ignored). Limitation: because the name search loop uses offset < strtab_size - 6, a ".data\0" occupying the last 6 bytes of the string table is not found and the default is returned.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R17): off-by-one at line 81 (offset < strtab_size - 6 excludes the last position); slice cut head, real name find_elf_data_sec (line 745)

name: archive_read_support_format_by_code
prose: int archive_read_support_format_by_code(struct archive *a, int format_code). Precondition: a must be a valid archive handle (an invalid handle makes __archive_check_magic print a diagnostic and terminate the process via diediedie). Postcondition: archive_check_magic runs first: if a->magic is not ARCHIVE_READ_MAGIC, or the state does not include ARCHIVE_STATE_NEW, an error is set, the state is set to fatal and the function returns ARCHIVE_FATAL at once (it does not terminate). Otherwise, if (format_code & ARCHIVE_FORMAT_BASE_MASK) equals one of the 15 supported base codes (7ZIP, AR, CAB, CPIO, EMPTY, ISO9660, LHA, MTREE, RAR, RAR_V5, RAW, TAR, WARC, XAR, ZIP) it returns exactly the value of the corresponding archive_read_support_format_* call; for any other code it sets error ARCHIVE_ERRNO_PROGRAMMER 'Invalid format code specified' on a and returns ARCHIVE_FATAL.
note: reviewers: R15 (archive_check_magic does not terminate for a wrong magic/state; it returns ARCHIVE_FATAL via the macro) RIGHT, R2 (aborts) WRONG except for an invalid handle (archive_check_magic.c:146-153)

name: cab_consume_cfdata
prose: static int64_t cab_consume_cfdata(struct archive_read *a, int64_t consumed_bytes) (archive_read_support_format_cab.c lines 196-283). Precondition: a is a CAB reader with cab->entry_cfdata, entry_cffile and entry_cffolder set; consumed_bytes >= 0. Postcondition: it first calls cab_minimum_consume_cfdata(a, consumed_bytes); a negative result returns ARCHIVE_FATAL. Then, while bytes remain to be consumed: if the current CFDATA has compressed_size 0 it sets 'Invalid CFDATA' and returns ARCHIVE_FATAL. cbytes is min(uncompressed_bytes_remaining, remaining). If nothing of this CFDATA has been decompressed yet (uncompressed_avail == 0) and the file's folder is iFoldCONTINUED_PREV_AND_NEXT or iFoldCONTINUED_FROM_PREV: when cbytes covers the whole CFDATA it consumes the compressed bytes without decompressing, zeroes the remaining counters and calls cab_next_cfdata (a negative result is returned as is); if the new CFDATA has uncompressed size 0 and the folder is PREV_AND_NEXT, TO_NEXT or FROM_PREV, the remaining count is set to 0 and the function ends normally (no error); when cbytes covers only part, read_offset and uncompressed_bytes_remaining are adjusted and the loop ends. Otherwise, if cbytes == 0 (current CFDATA exhausted) it calls cab_next_cfdata (a negative result is returned as is) and, if the new CFDATA has uncompressed size 0 and the folder is PREV_AND_NEXT, TO_NEXT or FROM_PREV, it returns ARCHIVE_FATAL without setting an archive error. Otherwise it decompresses through cab_read_ahead_cfdata and consumes in a loop; if no data is available (avail <= 0) or cab_minimum_consume_cfdata fails it returns ARCHIVE_FATAL (the error, if any, was set by the callee). On normal completion it returns consumed_bytes.
note: reviewers: R1 (zero-size next CFDATA in cbytes==0 branch returns FATAL without setting an error) RIGHT; R15 (skip-whole branch instead sets remaining to 0 and returns consumed_bytes) RIGHT

name: zisofs_read_data
prose: static int zisofs_read_data(struct archive_read *a, const void **buff, size_t *size, int64_t *offset), the HAVE_ZLIB_H definition (archive_read_support_format_iso9660.c lines 1498-1718; slice shows most of it). Precondition: the current entry is zisofs-compressed with consistent entry_zisofs state. Postcondition: it read-aheads at least 1 byte (none -> error 'Truncated zisofs file body', ARCHIVE_FATAL) and limits the input to entry_bytes_remaining. While the zisofs header/block-pointer table are not fully read it copies from the input to fill them: a bad header (magic, size, byte 12 != 4, log2 block size mismatch) gives 'Illegal zisofs file body' and ARCHIVE_FATAL; memory allocation failures give ARCHIVE_FATAL with ENOMEM; if the table is still incomplete it produces 0 output bytes. Once initialised, when starting a new block it reads a pair of offsets: too few pointers, an offset that does not equal the current position, or an end offset before the start gives ARCHIVE_FATAL ('Illegal zisofs block pointers'); inflateInit/inflateReset failure gives ARCHIVE_FATAL. A zero-length block produces a zero-filled buffer of uncompressed_buffer_size; otherwise inflate is run on the available block bytes (a result other than Z_OK or Z_STREAM_END gives ARCHIVE_FATAL 'zisofs decompression failed'). On success it sets *buff to the internal buffer, *size to the number of bytes produced (possibly 0), *offset to the sparse offset, advances entry_sparse_offset, entry_bytes_remaining, current_position and pz_offset by the input bytes used, and adds that number to entry_bytes_unconsumed, so the input is consumed later by the next read_data call (not here); it returns ARCHIVE_OK.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): input is only deferred through entry_bytes_unconsumed (line 192), consumed on the next read_data call (lines 223-226)

name: zisofs_read_data
prose: static int zisofs_read_data(struct archive_read *a, const void **buff, size_t *size, int64_t *offset), the definition used when HAVE_ZLIB_H is not defined (archive_read_support_format_iso9660.c lines 1722-1733). Postcondition: leaves *buff, *size and *offset untouched, sets an ARCHIVE_ERRNO_FILE_FORMAT error 'zisofs is not supported on this platform' on a->archive, and returns ARCHIVE_FAILED.
note: verified; the no-zlib stub returns ARCHIVE_FAILED (R1 claim consistent)

name: archive_read_format_lha_read_header
prose: static int archive_read_format_lha_read_header(struct archive_read *a, struct archive_entry *entry) (archive_read_support_format_lha.c lines 473-746; slice cut head). Precondition: a->format->data is a struct lha; entry is a valid archive_entry. Postcondition: it resets per-entry decompression state and tries to read ahead the fixed header size; if that fails it reads ahead one byte and returns ARCHIVE_EOF when no byte is available or the byte is 0, otherwise truncated_error(a). For an 'MZ' file before the first header it skips the SFX stub with lha_skip_sfx (returning any error below ARCHIVE_WARN) and reads ahead a byte (truncated_error on failure). A zero first byte returns ARCHIVE_EOF; a header format check failure sets 'Bad LHa file' and returns ARCHIVE_FATAL. It then initialises the entry defaults from the header level (0-3 handled by the level-specific readers; another level sets an error and ARCHIVE_FATAL) and returns the reader's error if it is below ARCHIVE_WARN. A non-directory with an empty filename returns truncated_error(a). It converts the directory and file names to wide characters separately (a conversion failure sets an error, frees the temporary strings and returns ARCHIVE_FATAL), concatenates them, for a symlink parses the link target (failure sets 'Unknown symlink-name', frees the strings and returns ARCHIVE_FAILED) and otherwise forces the file type; sets read-only mode bits from DOS attributes when no Unix mode was given; fills the entry pathname, symlink, mode, uid/gid, uname/gname, times and size (unset for directories and symlinks); sets entry_bytes_remaining from compsize (negative -> 'Invalid LHa entry size', ARCHIVE_FATAL), marks end_of_entry for directories and zero-size content, sets the format name, and returns the level reader's status, ARCHIVE_OK or ARCHIVE_WARN.
note: reviewers R15 and R17 WRONG: when no data remains at all the code returns ARCHIVE_EOF (lines 498-505); truncated_error is returned only when some bytes remain but fewer than the header size

name: read_header
prose: static int read_header(struct archive_read *a, struct archive_entry *entry) in archive_read_support_format_mtree.c (lines 1120-1174). Precondition: a->format->data is a struct mtree; entry is a valid archive_entry. Postcondition: it closes mtree->fd if it was open. On first use (entries == NULL) it creates a link resolver (NULL -> ARCHIVE_FATAL), sets its strategy, and calls read_mtree, returning its status if it is not ARCHIVE_OK. It copies the archive format and format name from mtree. Then it loops over the entries: no current entry -> ARCHIVE_EOF; a '..' entry is marked used and the current_dir path loses its last component; an entry that is not yet used is passed to parse_file with a use_next flag: if use_next is 0 the status r from parse_file (ARCHIVE_OK or an error/warning code) is returned and this_entry is not advanced (the entry is marked used by parse_file); if use_next is set (an optional entry whose on-disk type did not match) the result r is discarded and the loop moves to the next entry. Entries already used are skipped.
note: reviewers: R1 (FATAL when the resolver cannot be allocated) RIGHT and R15 (use_next path discards parse_file's result and continues) RIGHT

name: readline
prose: static ssize_t readline(struct archive_read *a, struct mtree *mtree, char **start, ssize_t limit) (archive_read_support_format_mtree.c lines 2096-2175; slice shows the loop only). Precondition: mtree->line is an initialised archive_string owned by mtree, start is a valid pointer, limit is the maximum accepted line size. Postcondition: it repeatedly reads ahead at least one byte, trims the chunk to end at the first newline, and fails with ARCHIVE_FATAL ('Line too long', chunk not consumed) if the accumulated size plus the chunk plus 1 would exceed limit, or with ARCHIVE_FATAL ('Can't allocate working buffer', ENOMEM) if the buffer cannot grow; a negative bytes_read also gives ARCHIVE_FATAL. Otherwise the chunk is appended to mtree->line, consumed from the archive and NUL-terminated. It then scans the new part: an unescaped newline ends the line: if it is preceded by a carriage return the CR is replaced by the newline and the length reduced by one, *start is set to mtree->line.s and the length of the line including the trailing newline (excluding the NUL) is returned; a '#' with no newline yet read stops the scan so that more data is read; a backslash followed by a newline (or CR LF) removes those characters from the accumulated line and continues reading the next line as a continuation; any other backslash escape skips the following character. If read-ahead returns no data (end of file or error) it returns 0, and bytes already accumulated stay consumed.
note: slice cut head; old action was drop; real function is readline (mtree.c:2096); returned length includes the trailing newline per its header comment

name: xmllite_read_toc
prose: static int xmllite_read_toc(struct archive_read *a) (archive_read_support_format_xar.c lines 3558-3667, Windows XmlLite build). Precondition: a is a xar reader. Postcondition: it creates a stream adapter (a negative status is the return value; the adapter pointer stays NULL), creates an IXmlReader (failure -> ARCHIVE_FATAL without setting an archive error), sets the adapter as input (failure -> error 'Failed to prepare XML stream', ARCHIVE_FATAL) and loops until IsEOF: a Read failure sets 'Failed to read XML stream' and returns ARCHIVE_FATAL; for an element it gets its local name (NULL -> ARCHIVE_FATAL, error set by the helper), builds the attribute list with xmllite_xmlattr_setup and, if that returns ARCHIVE_OK, calls xml_start; the attribute list is cleaned up, xml_end is called for an empty element if r is OK, the name is freed, and any non-OK r (which can be a warning or failure code from the setup or xml_start, not only ARCHIVE_FATAL) ends the loop; for an end element it calls xml_end with the name; for text it gets the value (non-OK result ends the function), calls xml_data and frees the text buffer (archive_string_free is called) and then falls through to the ignored node types; other node types are ignored. On every path the reader, if created, is released and the adapter freed with free(). It returns r: ARCHIVE_OK when the loop ended at EOF with no error.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R17): the text buffer is freed at line 73 before falling through; slice cut head; real name xmllite_read_toc (line 3559)

name: init_WinZip_AES_decryption
prose: static int init_WinZip_AES_decryption(struct archive_read *a) (archive_read_support_format_zip.c lines 2985-3075). Precondition: zip->entry has aes_extra set. Postcondition: if zip->cctx_valid or zip->hctx_valid is already set it returns ARCHIVE_OK at once. A strength other than 1, 2 or 3 sets 'Corrupted ZIP file data' and returns ARCHIVE_FATAL; failure to read ahead salt_len + 2 bytes sets 'Truncated ZIP file data' and returns ARCHIVE_FATAL. It then loops over candidate passphrases from __archive_read_next_passphrase: none available returns ARCHIVE_FAILED ('Passphrase required for this entry', or 'Incorrect passphrase' after a retry); a PBKDF2 failure returns ARCHIVE_FAILED; a passphrase whose derived verification bytes match ends the loop; after more than 10000 wrong passphrases it returns ARCHIVE_FAILED. It then initialises the AES-CTR context (failure -> ARCHIVE_FAILED) and the HMAC-SHA1 context (failure -> releases the AES context, ARCHIVE_FAILED), marks cctx_valid and hctx_valid, consumes salt_len + 2 bytes, subtracts salt_len + 2 + AUTH_CODE_SIZE from entry_bytes_remaining and, only if ZIP_LENGTH_AT_END is not set in the entry's flags and entry_bytes_remaining is now negative, sets 'Corrupted ZIP file data' and returns ARCHIVE_FATAL (leaving the contexts initialised and marked valid and the header consumed). Otherwise it adds the same amount to entry_compressed_bytes_read, zeroes decrypted_bytes_remaining, sets the entry compression from aes_extra.compression and returns zip_alloc_decryption_buffer(a), which returns ARCHIVE_FATAL on allocation failure (the contexts again stay initialised) or ARCHIVE_OK.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the negative-remaining check applies only without ZIP_LENGTH_AT_END (lines 3058-3060); R1 claim (contexts left initialised on buffer failure) RIGHT

name: restore_entry
prose: static int restore_entry(struct archive_write_disk *a) (archive_write_disk_posix.c lines 2077-2267). Precondition: a describes the entry (name, mode, flags, entry). Postcondition: if ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_UNLINK is set and the new object is not a directory it tries unlink (success clears a->pst), tolerates ENOENT, tries rmdir (success clears a->pst) and otherwise returns ARCHIVE_FAILED ('Could not unlink'). It then calls create_filesystem_object, and for ENOTDIR/ENOENT (unless NO_AUTODIR) creates the parent directories and tries again. ENOENT for a hard link returns ARCHIVE_FAILED ('Hard-link target ... does not exist'). EISDIR/EEXIST with ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_NO_OVERWRITE returns ARCHIVE_OK (after zeroing a->todo for a directory and unsetting the entry size). EISDIR: rmdir (failure -> ARCHIVE_FAILED), clears a->pst and retries. EEXIST: it stats the existing object (failure -> ARCHIVE_FAILED); with NO_OVERWRITE_NEWER and a non-directory that is not older it unsets the size and returns ARCHIVE_OK; if it is the archive being read it returns ARCHIVE_FAILED ('Refusing to overwrite archive'); an existing non-directory is replaced either by a temporary file (SAFE_WRITES and a regular file: a->fd = la_mktemp, failure -> ARCHIVE_FAILED, a->pst cleared, en = 0) or by unlink (failure -> ARCHIVE_FAILED) and a retry (a->pst cleared); an existing directory with a non-directory entry is removed with rmdir (failure -> ARCHIVE_FAILED) and the creation retried, without clearing a->pst at that point; an existing directory for a directory entry only schedules a deferred mode fix when the modes differ and TODO_MODE_FORCE is set, and the EEXIST is forgotten. If an error remains it sets a 'Can't create' error if none is set and returns ARCHIVE_FAILED; otherwise it clears a->pst and returns ARCHIVE_OK. The only return codes are ARCHIVE_OK and ARCHIVE_FAILED.
note: reviewers: R1 (NO_OVERWRITE_NEWER and dir-over-dir OK returns) covered; R15 (a->pst not cleared when rmdir of an existing dir succeeds and the retry fails, lines 2234-2240 then 2257-2262) RIGHT: old claim 'cleared on every path that created or removed an object' was wrong

name: _7z_write_header
prose: static int _7z_write_header(struct archive_write *a, struct archive_entry *entry) (archive_write_set_format_7zip.c lines 559-662). Precondition: a->format_data is a struct _7zip; entry is a valid archive entry (it is never modified or freed). Postcondition: it clears zip->cur_file and entry_bytes_remaining; if the UTF-16LE string conversion cannot be created it returns ARCHIVE_FATAL. It calls file_new; a result below ARCHIVE_WARN frees the file (if any) and is returned. A zero-size directory already present in the red-black tree is freed and ARCHIVE_OK returned with no counters updated. Otherwise it updates the time counters, total_number_entry and total_bytes_entry_name; a zero-size entry also bumps the empty-entry (and directory) counters, registers an empty file, and returns file_new's status (ARCHIVE_OK or ARCHIVE_WARN). For a non-empty entry it initialises the compression encoder when this is the first non-empty entry (with ZSTD support an out-of-range compression level, or an encoder initialisation failure, frees the file and returns ARCHIVE_FATAL; the counters have already been updated by then), registers the file, sets cur_file, entry_bytes_remaining and the CRC, and for a symlink writes the link target as content with compress_out (a negative result is returned after the file has been registered, with cur_file set); finally it returns file_new's status.
note: reviewers: R1 (file freed, not the entry) RIGHT; R15 (counters already updated before compression-init failure; symlink write failure returns after registration) RIGHT

name: write_global
prose: static void write_global(struct mtree_writer *mtree) (archive_write_set_format_mtree.c lines 436-564). Precondition: mtree->acs holds the attribute counter lists (uid_list, gid_list, mode_list, flags_list, possibly NULL) and mtree->set describes what the last /set line established. Postcondition: keys = mtree->keys & SET_KEYS and effkeys start equal; if a /set has been written before (set.processing) the type key is dropped from effkeys and each of uid/uname, gid/gname, mode and flags is dropped from effkeys when its list is NULL, or when it was previously set and the top counter has a count below 2 or the same value as the saved one; if no /set was written yet the keys whose lists are NULL are dropped from keys. For keys in keys & effkeys it builds a set string: ' type=dir' or ' type=file' (also setting set.type), ' uname=' only when the top entry's uname is non-empty (otherwise F_UNAME is removed from keys and, only when oldkeys had F_UNAME, ' uname' is added to the unset string), ' uid=' (setting set.uid), the same for gname and gid, ' mode=%o' (setting set.mode), and ' flags=' with fflags_set/fflags_clear saved when the flags text is non-empty (otherwise F_FLAGS is removed from keys and ' flags' is added to the unset string only if oldkeys had F_FLAGS). It appends '/unset%s\n' to mtree->buf only if the unset string is non-empty and then '/set%s\n' only if the set string is non-empty, frees both strings, stores the remaining keys in mtree->set.keys and sets set.processing = 1. Returns nothing.
note: reviewers: R1 (lines only appended when non-empty) and R15 (unset name added only if oldkeys had that key) RIGHT

name: archive_write_pax_header
prose: static int archive_write_pax_header(struct archive_write *a, struct archive_entry *entry_original) (archive_write_set_format_pax.c lines 577-1538; read in full except the callees). Precondition: a->format_data is a struct pax; entry_original is a valid entry. Postcondition: returns ARCHIVE_FAILED with an error if the entry has no pathname, or if the UTF-8 conversion object cannot be created (non-binary mode). It chooses the header charset and translates the hardlink name (a conversion failure retries without conversion, sets a warning and switches to binary mode; ARCHIVE_FATAL is returned at once). If there is no hardlink it checks the file type: block, char, FIFO, symlink and regular files pass; for a directory it appends a '/' to the pathname of entry_original (so the caller's entry is modified; an allocation failure returns ARCHIVE_FATAL); sockets and unknown types set an error and return ARCHIVE_FAILED; this type check is skipped entirely when a hardlink name is present. If the entry carries Mac metadata it recursively writes a '._' companion entry plus its data (errors below ARCHIVE_WARN are returned, warnings are merged into the result). It clones the entry (NULL -> ARCHIVE_FATAL), collects sparse information, translates pathname, uname, gname and symlink names (FATAL on allocation failure, otherwise a conversion failure sets a warning and binary mode with the hdrcharset BINARY attribute), and builds pax attributes for long or non-ASCII paths and link names, large uid/gid/size/device numbers, times, fflags, ACLs (the status of add_pax_acl assigns ret, which can replace an earlier warning), sparse maps, extended attributes (FATAL aborts) and symlink type. It sets the size to 0 for non-regular entries and hardlinks, formats the ustar header for the main entry (FATAL aborts), and, when attributes exist, writes an 'x' extended header entry first (header formatting failure, or any output failure, returns ARCHIVE_FATAL; sparse list cleared on the first output failure). It then writes the main 512-byte header (a failed output returns that error code), sets the caller's entry size to the real size, registers the data as a single sparse block for non-sparse files, sets the padding and returns ret, which is ARCHIVE_OK or the lowest ARCHIVE_WARN-level status seen. The cloned entry and temporary name string are freed on every return after they are created.
note: old action was drop; real function is archive_write_pax_header (line 577); reviewer R2 RIGHT: no type check when hardlink != NULL; ARCHIVE_FATAL also returned for output failures; I read lines 577-1538 fully but not the callees (get_entry_*, add_pax_acl, header_ustar)

name: archive_write_zip_header
prose: static int archive_write_zip_header(struct archive_write *a, struct archive_entry *entry) (archive_write_set_format_zip.c lines 791-1499; slice cut head). Precondition: a->format_data is a struct zip. Postcondition: it returns ARCHIVE_FAILED, before changing any per-entry zip state, if the entry has no pathname, its file type is not regular, directory or symlink, or ZIP_FLAG_AVOID_ZIP64 is set and the entry size or zip->written_bytes exceeds the 4 GB limit. It then sets the entry size to 0 for non-regular files (modifying the caller's entry), resets the per-entry state (offsets, sizes, flags, crc, encryption, previously stored entry freed, crypto contexts released and cleared), and, for a non-empty regular file, marks it encrypted if encryption was requested. It clones the entry (failure -> ARCHIVE_FATAL), converts the pathname to the zip charset (ENOMEM -> ARCHIVE_FATAL; other failure with an MBS pathname -> warning ARCHIVE_WARN and the raw pathname is used; failure with no MBS pathname -> ARCHIVE_FAILED, after the per-entry state has been reset and zip->entry set to the clone), converts a symlink target (ENOMEM -> ARCHIVE_FATAL, other failures ignored), sets the UTF-8 flag if needed, and computes compression, sizes, version-needed and flags for symlinks, other non-regular files and regular files with or without a known size. It formats the local header and the central-directory header in memory (the central directory entry counter is incremented and its buffers allocated), builds the extra fields, and writes the 30-byte local header, the path, the extra data and, for symlinks, the link target to the output; any output failure returns ARCHIVE_FATAL. It then initialises the chosen compressor (deflate, bzip2, zstd, lzma or xz when built in; a failed init sets ENOMEM and returns ARCHIVE_FATAL) and returns ARCHIVE_OK or ARCHIVE_WARN (from the pathname conversion). The central directory record is not written here; it is only accumulated in memory.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): pathname-translation failure without an MBS name returns ARCHIVE_FAILED after the state reset; old prose also wrongly said the central-directory header is written here (it is only built in memory); I read lines 791-1499

name: DEFINE_TEST(test_read_format_gtar_filename_KOI8R_UTF8)
prose: Generated function body for DEFINE_TEST(test_read_format_gtar_filename_KOI8R_UTF8) (test_read_format_gtar_filename.c lines 240-290; slice cut head). It then tests (not asserts) archive_read_set_options(a, "hdrcharset=KOI8-R"): if that does not return ARCHIVE_OK it reports skipping that the system cannot convert KOI8-R to UTF-8 and jumps to the cleanup label. Otherwise it asserts that archive_read_open_filename returns ARCHIVE_OK, that the first two archive_read_next_header calls return ARCHIVE_OK with pathnames "\xd0\xbf\xd1\x80\xd0\xb8\xd0\xb2\xd0\xb5\xd1\x82" and "\xd0\x9f\xd0\xa0\xd0\x98\xd0\x92\xd0\x95\xd0\xa2" and size 6, that the third call returns ARCHIVE_EOF, that archive_filter_code(a, 0) is ARCHIVE_FILTER_COMPRESS, archive_format(a) is ARCHIVE_FORMAT_TAR_GNUTAR and archive_read_close returns ARCHIVE_OK. name: bsdtar_getopt
prose: int bsdtar_getopt(struct bsdtar *bsdtar) (libarchive tar/cmdline.c lines 199-410; slice cut head). Precondition: bsdtar->argv is a NULL-terminated array with argc matching, getopt_state is 0 on the first call and otherwise the state of the previous call. Postcondition: on the first call the program name is skipped; if no words remain it returns -1; if the first word does not begin with '-' it is taken as an old-style group of option letters (e.g. 'xbf'), consumed from argv, and one letter is returned per call: a letter not in the short option table returns '?' with no warning; a letter taking an argument (a ':' follows it in the table) takes the next argv word as bsdtar->argument, or prints a warning and returns '?' when no word is left; after the letters are exhausted normal parsing continues. In normal parsing it returns -1 when no words remain, when the next word does not begin with '-', or when the next word is "--" (consumed). A word starting with '-' is a group of short options, one per call: an unknown letter returns '?' silently; a letter with a required argument takes the rest of the word (run-in) or the next word (warning and '?' if there is none); the ':' character itself matches the option table and is returned as ':' (it is not rejected). -W takes its argument as a long option name. A word starting with '--' is matched against the table of long options (prefix match, up to '='): an unsupported or ambiguous name, a missing required argument, or an argument given to an option that forbids one produces a lafe_warnc warning and returns '?'; a unique match returns its equivalent value (a short letter or an OPTION_* code) and sets bsdtar->argument. argv and argc advance by the words consumed and getopt_state/getopt_word are updated to resume parsing.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): unknown short options return '?' without a warning (lines 248-249, 308-309); I also noted that ':' is accepted (strchr matches the ':' of 'b:') and old-style mode, which the old prose omitted

name: test_run
prose: static int test_run(int i, const char *tmpdir) in libarchive's test_main.c (lines 118-264). Precondition: i is a valid index into the tests array and tmpdir is the top-level work directory. Postcondition: it prints a header line according to verbosity, then calls exit(1) after printing an error if any of these fail: chdir to tmpdir, formatting the log file name (error or truncation), formatting the per-test work directory path (error or truncation), creating the per-test work directory, chown to the test user (RUN_TEST_UNPRIV), or chdir into it. It opens the log file with fopen without checking the result, sets the C locale, saves the umask, optionally drops privileges (RUN_TEST_UNPRIV), runs tests[i].func(), restores the credentials and umask, resets the locale, and chdirs back to tmpdir (exit(1) on failure). It stores the number of failures added by the test in tests[i].failures, calls test_summarize, closes the log file and sets logfile to NULL. If that number is 0, keep_temp_files is false and a second assertChdir(tmpdir) succeeds, it removes the per-test directory and the log file with systemf (results ignored); otherwise they are kept. It returns tests[i].failures.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): removal also requires the second assertChdir(tmpdir) to succeed (line 240); also fopen of the log is unchecked (line 164) and the locale is not saved/restored (R1 RIGHT)

name: main
prose: int main(int argc, char **argv) of the libarchive test harness (test_main.c lines 3976-4416; I read the whole function and usage/get_refdir/get_test_set, not the other callees). Postcondition: it gets the current directory, derives progname and testprogdir from argv[0] (a failed malloc or realloc there prints a message and exits with status 1), reads TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP/TEMPDIR, ENVBASE_DEBUG, _VERBOSITY_LEVEL (an out-of-range value is silently replaced by VERBOSITY_PASSFAIL) and ENVBASE_TEST_FILES, and parses options -d, -k, -l (list tests and exit(0)), -p, -q, -r, -s, -u, -v (and -U with RUN_TEST_UNPRIV): a missing argument for -p/-r, an unrecognised option, or -p when PROGRAM is not defined prints a message and calls usage(), which ends the process with exit(1). With PROGRAM defined it builds the tested program path (exit(1) if the malloc for it fails; the malloc of the quoted copy testprg is not checked), and rejects a relative refdir (non-Windows) with exit(1). It ignores SIGPIPE, with RUN_TEST_UNPRIV looks up the target user when running as root (exit(1) if unknown), and creates a timestamped temp directory (exit(1) if the path is too long or none can be created within 1000 attempts). get_refdir may also end the process with exit(1) when the reference files are not found. It prints a banner, then runs the selected tests (an invalid test selection prints '*** INVALID Test', frees memory and calls usage() which exits with 1; with -u it repeats until a test fails). It prints the totals and failing tests, frees tmp2, testprogdir, pwd and refdir_alloc, does chdir("..") and rmdir(tmpdir), and returns 1 if any test failed (a test whose test_run result was nonzero), otherwise 2 if fail_if_tests_skipped is set and skips > 0, otherwise 0.

name: bsdunzip_getopt
prose: int bsdunzip_getopt(struct bsdunzip *bsdunzip) (libarchive unzip/cmdline.c lines 61-235). Short options are "aCcd:fI:jLlnO:opP:qtuvx:yZ:" and the only long option is "version" (no argument, equivalent OPTION_VERSION). Postcondition: on the first call the program name is skipped; it returns -1 when no words remain, when the next word does not begin with '-', or when the word is "--" (consumed, with bsdunzip_optind incremented). A word starting with a single '-' is parsed as a group of short options, one per call: a letter not found in the table returns '?' silently (no warning); a letter followed by ':' in the table takes the rest of the word or the next word as bsdunzip->argument (a warning and '?' if there is no next word); the ':' character itself is found in the table (strchr matches the ':' after 'd', 'I', 'O', 'P', 'x', 'Z') and is returned as ':' rather than '?'. A word starting with '--' is looked up in the long table (up to '='): unsupported or ambiguous names, or an argument given to an option that forbids one, print a lafe_warnc warning and return '?'; a unique match returns OPTION_VERSION. argv, argc and bsdunzip_optind advance by each consumed word, and the parser state is saved for the next call.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): ':' is accepted as an option letter via strchr on short_options (line 135-139); R1 (unknown short option silent) RIGHT

name: operator new(size_t size, const std::nothrow_t &)
prose: void *operator new(size_t size, const std::nothrow_t &) (libcxxrt memory.cc, weak definition). Precondition: none. Postcondition: it returns noexcept_new<operator new>(size): the result of the corresponding throwing operator new (which uses malloc, treating a zero size as 1, and loops calling the new handler until malloc succeeds), or, when exceptions are enabled, nullptr if that call throws any exception (std::bad_alloc when there is no handler, or any exception thrown by the new handler); when _CXXRT_NO_EXCEPTIONS is defined the throwing version is called directly without a try block, and with no handler it returns nullptr (it breaks out of the loop). The result must be released with operator delete.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): this is the nothrow variant; noexcept_new catches every exception and returns nullptr (memory.cc:88-104); the throwing version is the separate operator new

name: operator new[](size_t size, const std::nothrow_t &)
prose: void *operator new[](size_t size, const std::nothrow_t &) (libcxxrt memory.cc, weak definition). Precondition: none. Postcondition: it returns noexcept_new<operator new[]>(size): the result of the corresponding throwing operator new[] (which forwards to operator new) (which uses malloc, treating a zero size as 1, and loops calling the new handler until malloc succeeds), or, when exceptions are enabled, nullptr if that call throws any exception (std::bad_alloc when there is no handler, or any exception thrown by the new handler); when _CXXRT_NO_EXCEPTIONS is defined the throwing version is called directly without a try block, and with no handler it returns nullptr (it breaks out of the loop). The result must be released with operator delete[].
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): nothrow variant wraps the throwing operator new[] with noexcept_new

name: libder_obj_normalize
prose: LIBDER_PRIVATE bool libder_obj_normalize(struct libder_object *obj, struct libder_ctx *ctx) (libder_obj.c lines 75-169; slice cut head). Precondition: obj is a valid object with type metadata and ctx is a valid context. Postcondition: for a constructed type, if constructed normalization is enabled for ctx it first calls libder_obj_coalesce_children and returns false if that fails; if the object is still constructed it recursively normalizes each child (returning false on the first child failure), returns true for any type other than SET, and for a SET returns the result of libder_obj_normalize_set (false with LDE_NOMEM recorded when the temporary calloc fails; otherwise the children are sorted and relinked). A non-universal or tag-encoded object, or a type for which libder_normalizing_type is false for ctx, is returned unchanged with true. For the remaining universal primitive types: BIT STRING, BOOLEAN and INTEGER with a NULL payload only get their length set to 1; a NULL object frees any payload and sets payload NULL and length 0; other types with a NULL payload are unchanged; BIT STRING (clear the unused bits), BOOLEAN (collapse to one byte 0x00/0xff) and INTEGER (strip redundant leading bytes) call their helpers, which always return true; every other type is unchanged and true is returned.
note: reviewers RIGHT: R1 (normalization depends on ctx/type enabling) and R15 (false return from libder_obj_normalize_set when calloc fails, lines 51-55)

name: cv_delfini
prose: libedit_private void cv_delfini(EditLine *el) (libedit chared.c lines 338-370). Precondition: el is a valid EditLine in the middle of a vi delete or yank command. Postcondition: if the pending action has the INSERT bit, the current key map is reset to el_map.key. If c_vcmd.pos is 0 the function then returns with the action unchanged and nothing deleted or yanked. Otherwise size = cursor - pos; if that is 0 it is forced to 1. The cursor is set to pos. With the YANK bit the region is yanked: size > 0 yanks size characters starting at pos, otherwise (size < 0) yanks -size characters starting at the old cursor position (pos + size). Without YANK: size > 0 deletes size characters after the cursor (at pos) and refreshes the cursor; size < 0 deletes -size characters before the cursor and moves the cursor back by -size (to the old cursor). Finally c_vcmd.action is set to NOP. A zero-length region therefore deletes or yanks one character at the position.
note: reviewers: R1 (early return leaves action unreset) RIGHT, already stated; R15 (zero size forced to 1) RIGHT (lines 351-353)

name: fn_complete2
prose: int fn_complete2(EditLine *el, complete_func, attempted_completion_function, word_break, special_prefixes, app_func, query_items, completion_type, over, point, end, flags) (libedit filecomplete.c lines 659-827). Precondition: el is valid; word_break is a NUL-terminated wide string; special_prefixes may be NULL; complete_func, app_func, completion_type, over, point and end may be NULL (defaults fn_filename_completion_function and append_char_function are used for the first two). Postcondition: what_to_do is '\t', or '?' when the last command equals the current one, and is stored through completion_type if non-NULL. It finds the word before the cursor; if there is none it returns CC_NORM without setting point, end or over. Otherwise it stores the cursor and lastchar offsets through point and end when non-NULL, obtains matches from attempted_completion_function (if given) and, if there is none or it returned NULL while *over was 0, from completion_matches; it sets *over to 0 when over is non-NULL. With no matches it returns CC_NORM. Otherwise the return value starts as CC_REFRESH; if the common prefix matches[0] is non-empty it deletes the word from the line and inserts the (escaped when FN_QUOTE_MATCH is set) prefix, adding the app_func suffix when there is a single match, an attempted_completion_function and FN_QUOTE_MATCH is not set; if the copy of the prefix cannot be allocated the word has already been deleted and the function returns CC_REFRESH after freeing the matches. When there are several matches and what_to_do is '!' or '?', it prints a newline, asks 'Display all N possibilities? (y or n)' reading stdin when N exceeds query_items, prints the list unless declined, and returns CC_REDISPLAY. Otherwise it beeps; with an empty common prefix it returns CC_NORM, else CC_REFRESH. The match array and its elements and the word copy are freed on all paths after they were obtained.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R1): point/end/over are not set when the word is not found (lines 692-693); added unlisted detail: word deleted before the escape/strdup allocation (lines 728-735)

name: hist_get
prose: libedit_private el_action_t hist_get(EditLine *el) (hist.c lines 100-160). Precondition: el has initialised history and line buffers. Postcondition: if el_history.eventno == 0 it copies the saved history buffer back into the line buffer, sets lastchar from el_history.last and puts the cursor at the start in vi mode (KSHVI) or at the end otherwise, and returns CC_REFRESH regardless of whether a history reference exists. If eventno != 0: a NULL history reference or an empty history returns CC_ERROR with eventno unchanged. Otherwise it walks to the eventno-th entry; if the walk runs off the end it sets eventno to the last event number reached and returns CC_ERROR; if the line buffer cannot be enlarged (ch_enlargebufs) for the entry it returns CC_ERROR with eventno unchanged (still equal to the requested number). On success it copies the entry into the line buffer, sets lastchar after it (dropping one trailing newline and then one trailing space), places the cursor (start in vi mode, otherwise at the end) and returns CC_REFRESH.
note: reviewers: R1 (CC_ERROR cases) RIGHT; R15 (eventno == 0 returns CC_REFRESH even with NULL ref or empty history) RIGHT (lines 107-121); eventno on enlarge failure equals the requested value (h == eventno after the loop)
